newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul non-performing assets up from Q4.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul non-performing assets up from Q4.

text.p: St. Paul Bancorp Inc said Tuesday its non-performing assets as of March 31 totaled $20.8 million, or 0.46 percent of total assets, down from a year earlier but up from December 31, 1996.
A year-earlier, non-performing assets totalled $30.6 million, or 0.74 percent of total assets. At December 31, 1996, they totalled $12.5 million, or 0.29 percent.
The majority of the increase since December is attributable to one multi-family loan, it said.
St. Paul Bancorp said the nonperforming assets are still among the lowest in its recent history.
"We have been able to grow earning assets while maintaining our asset quality," Joseph Scully, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The company said it recorded no provision for loan losses during the first quarter, compared with a $500,000 provision in the first quarter of 1996.

St. Paul Bancorp said that through April 14 it had repurchased 561,750 shares, leaving about 450,000 shares to be repurchased under a board-approved program. During 1996 it bought back 1,268,750 shares.

The company's assets toatled $4.5 billion at March 31, up from $4.1 billion a year ago. Deposits were $3.4 billion, up from $3.3 billion. Loans receivable amounted to $3.0 billion, up from $2.8 billion.
